newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PAKISTAN COTTON RATES RISE AFTER RAINS IN SINDH.
newsitem.headline: PAKISTAN COTTON RATES RISE AFTER RAINS IN SINDH.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates for the new 1997/98 (July-June) crop rose on Saturday after rains in Sindh province and are likely to remain firm in the coming days on fears of a delay of new arrivals, dealers said.

"Recent rains in Sindh are good for the crop, but they have pushed up the cotton prices because the arrival of fresh supplies will be delayed now," dealer Kishan Chand said. "The roads leading to cotton-growing areas are bad and cotton transportaion comes to a halt during rains."
He said mills were piling up stocks on fears of a slowdown in supplies.
In the kerb market, the new-crop NIAB-78 variety was traded around 2,300 rupees ($56.62) per maund (37.32 k.g).
